Ordinary staff or students shall be able to submit requests.
Ordinary staff or students shall not manage inventory directly.
The main users of the system shall include staff, lecturers, and, in some cases, students.
Users shall be able to request equipment, software access, or room reservations.
Non-admin users shall have limited permissions compared with inventory administrators.
Non-admin users shall be able to cancel a request if it has not been approved yet.
An asset is any tracked item or resource that the university manages.
An asset can include a room, software licence, laptop, projector, or lab equipment.
A reservation is a time-based booking for something such as a room or shared equipment.
A request is a general ask for access, use, or allocation that may need approval before it becomes active.
Approval means the responsible office at the appropriate level has reviewed the request and accepted or rejected it.
At the department level, department inventory staff shall keep asset records up to date.
The system shall distinguish between a request and a reservation.
The system shall distinguish between ownership and custodianship.
The system shall use consistent labels so that each faculty does not describe the same thing in different ways.
The system shall enforce standard labels across the university to keep the core workflow consistent.
The system shall display short definitions or tooltips in the interface.
Emergency requests shall use a faster approval path.
Emergency requests shall allow limited overrides for authorized staff.
Cross-faculty sharing shall be tracked in the system.
Cross-faculty sharing shall require approval from both the lending side and the receiving side.
If ownership is unclear, cross-faculty sharing shall require approval from a higher-level approver.
Lending to external parties shall require special authorization.
Lending to external parties shall be disabled by default unless central administration allows it.
Some requests shall require more than one sign-off.
Requests shall require additional sign-offs when the item is shared across departments or has a high value.
The system shall support conditional approvals based on asset type.
The system shall handle room bookings differently from borrowing equipment or assigning software licences in its approval process.
The system shall allow automated approval for low-risk requests.
Automated approval shall not bypass oversight.
The interface shall use simple one-line explanations as the default tooltip format.
The system shall provide slightly richer pop-up tooltips for a few key terms such as request and reservation.
The interface shall keep tooltips lightweight so that the interface stays clean and does not feel cluttered.
The system shall provide brief examples in the tooltip for most cases.
The tooltip itself shall not include overly interactive content.
If a user needs more detail, the system shall allow the user to open a help page from the tooltip.
The system shall track users.
The system shall record ownership as the formal record of who ultimately controls an asset.
Approvals should usually go to the custodian or the relevant responsible unit first.
The system shall support reporting that shows both ownership and custodianship views.
The system shall use ownership for accountability and funding reporting.
The system shall use custodianship for operational responsibility and audits.
The inventory system shall integrate with HR and the university directory.
The inventory system shall support integration with room scheduling for reservations.
The inventory system shall support integration with finance or procurement data to help with asset ownership.
The inventory system shall support integration with finance or procurement data to help with cost centers.
The inventory system shall support integration with finance or procurement data to help with audit trails.
The inventory system shall support integration with software licence management.
The inventory system interfaces shall sync key data automatically.
The inventory system interfaces shall let approvers see the source of truth.
Important identity and role data should sync fairly frequently.
Less critical reference data should be updated on a scheduled basis.
If there is a discrepancy, the system should flag it rather than silently overwrite anything.
Administrators should receive alerts for failed syncs or conflicting records.
Regular users should see a simple message if something they need is temporarily unavailable.
The system shall interface with the university authentication service.
The system shall comply with university IT security standards.
The system shall handle staff information and possibly sensitive asset details.
The system shall fit within the university’s approved web and authentication platforms.
The system shall not introduce a separate login or an unsupported technology stack.
The system shall provide proper audit logging for approvals, changes, and access to records.
The system shall support records retention practices consistent with the university's internal governance policies.
The system shall treat external systems as authoritative for their own data domains.
The system shall not allow users to manually override synced fields except through a controlled admin process.
If a conflict or mismatch occurs during synchronization, the system shall quarantine the record or flag it for review rather than guessing.
The system shall apply the conflict-handling policy especially to user roles, room status, and asset identifiers.
The system shall implement retry logic for synchronization failures.
The system shall allow operations to continue with the last known good data until the issue is resolved.
External lending may occur occasionally and should be treated as an exceptional case.
When two systems disagree, the inventory system shall display the conflict clearly.
Every exception shall be logged.
The system shall implement role-based access control.
The system shall protect sensitive data and personal information in transit and at rest.
The system shall provide detailed audit logs for edits, approvals, deletions, and login or integration events.
The system should support peak usage of hundreds of concurrent users across the university.
The system should support an asset inventory in the tens of thousands, including rooms, equipment, and software licences.
The system should accommodate requests and reservations that vary significantly by term and department activity.
The system should be designed to grow without major changes.
The system should handle a combined inventory larger than any single faculty’s current system.
The system shall expect usage spikes at the start of term.
During usage spikes, the system shall remain responsive for search.
During usage spikes, non-urgent background tasks may slow down.
Normal user actions should feel quick.
The system shall degrade gracefully under load rather than failing outright.
The system should be sized to support a rough expectation rather than a firm peak-capacity number at this stage.
During the busiest periods, the system should support a few hundred concurrent users.
The system should support a few thousand active requests or reservations in flight at once across the university.
The capacity figures should be validated with the faculties before being finalized.
The system shall be available 24/7.
Planned maintenance shall be scheduled for low-usage times.
The system shall provide at least read-only access during planned maintenance if possible.
During unexpected outages, the system shall display a clear status message.
The system shall be designed to handle roughly 300 to 500 concurrent users at peak.
The system shall comfortably support an inventory size of tens of thousands of records.
The system shall include headroom in capacity planning rather than being sized too tightly to avoid later limits.
Planned maintenance should ideally be scheduled late at night or over a weekend when teaching and booking activity is lowest.
Users should receive a reminder shortly before the maintenance window starts.
If read-only access is not safe for the change being made, the system may have a short full downtime during maintenance.
Any short full downtime during maintenance should be clearly communicated.
During an unexpected outage, the system shall not expose technical details to users.
During an unexpected outage, the system shall send administrators specific alerts that include the scope of the problem.
During an unexpected outage, the system shall inform administrators whether bookings are affected.
During an unexpected outage, the system shall inform administrators whether approvals are affected.
During an unexpected outage, the system shall provide administrators an estimated recovery time when one is available.
The system shall provide read-only access so users can check room availability, asset details, and the status of their own requests.
The system shall not allow users to create new bookings during read-only mode.
The system shall not allow users to create approvals during read-only mode.
The system shall support extracting existing data from three different faculty systems.
The system shall support cleaning the extracted data before migration.
The system shall support mapping the cleaned data into one common structure before loading it into the new platform.
The migration process shall account for inconsistent naming in the source data as a risk.
The migration process shall account for duplicate assets in the source data as a risk.
The migration process shall account for missing records in the source data as a risk.
The migration process shall account for differences in how each faculty tracks rooms or licences as a risk.
The migration process shall account for old data being out of date as a risk.
The system shall include a clear validation step with each faculty before going live.
Each faculty shall review and sign off on the data it currently owns before migration.
The faculties shall agree on a shared template or mapping for the unified system.
The migration process shall include a trial import into a test environment.
Faculty administrators shall validate the results of the trial import.
The migration team shall fix mismatches or missing fields before the final load.
The actual import shall be controlled and reversible if possible.
The old systems shall have a short freeze on changes right before cutover.
Each faculty shall have a named contact.
The named contact in each faculty should preferably be an administration staff member who knows the faculty inventory well and can make decisions quickly.
Each faculty contact shall review validation reports from the test import.
Each faculty contact shall confirm which records are correct.
Each faculty contact shall flag duplicate records or records that should be retired.
The central team shall resolve flagged issues before the final load.
Each faculty shall provide written sign-off on its data set before go-live.
The migrated data must be signed off by all three faculties before full rollout.
The main workflow for asset lookup must pass user acceptance testing before full rollout.
The main workflow for requests must pass user acceptance testing before full rollout.
The main workflow for approvals must pass user acceptance testing before full rollout.
The main workflow for reservations must pass user acceptance testing before full rollout.
The system should be released through a short pilot or soft launch with one area or a limited group before full rollout.
User training and quick reference guides should be provided before full rollout.
